source.title: Optimize TSK Fuzzy Systems for Classification Problems: Minibatch Gradient Descent With Uniform Regularization and Batch Normalization
source.authors: Yuqi Cui; Dong-Rui Wu; Jian Huang

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies batch normalization to TSK fuzzy classifiers, a different model family, and reports its effects on training loss and test performance.
record.gate_note: The paper also cites prior work on batch normalization; those cited results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study extends BN to TSK fuzzy classifiers and evaluates its own method. V6 concerns neural networks; the study's fuzzy-system results do not test that version's specified system class. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately captures the authors' conclusion: consequent-input BN speeds convergence and improves generalization in TSK fuzzy classifiers, and combining BN with UR generally gives the best classification performance. This is an overall conclusion, not a claim of improvement on every dataset.
record.recipe_differences: Extends BN to TSK fuzzy classifiers; the study does not test the listed deep neural network recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper evaluates three BN placements. TSK-MBGD-UR-BN has the highest average BCA (0.7404), while TSK-MBGD-UR-GBN has the lowest (0.7106); TSK-MBGD-UR-RBN training is described as less stable.

fits_no_version.finding: On Satellite with UR weight 1, BN gives smaller early training losses and better test BCA in the reported 10-run averages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalizing inputs to TSK rule consequents can accelerate optimization and improve early test performance.

fits_no_version.finding: BN placement affects TSK performance: mean test BCA is 0.7404 for shared consequent BN, 0.7106 for global BN, and 0.7265 for rule-specific BN, versus 0.7121 without BN. Rule-specific BN training is described as less stable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefits of BN in TSK fuzzy classifiers depend on its placement.

record.problems: The BN convergence comparison is limited to the Satellite dataset and the first 20 epochs. Figure values are not reported numerically, and no uncertainty estimates are provided for the 10-run averages.

untested.parts: All parts: convolutional-network training classification error, dataset and label conditions, model size, and training recipes.
All parts: ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious minima, and extra student neurons.
All parts: depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
All parts: activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
All parts: stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature, recovery, and divergence.
All parts within the specified neural-network scope, including faster accuracy gains, higher learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The functional similarities discussed between fuzzy systems and neural networks do not establish that these experiments test the neural-network versions supplied here. Row states indicate inability to determine those versions, not absence of the reported fuzzy-system effects.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, and effects of model size or training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and spurious local minima.
Depth effects, identity shortcuts, plain networks, and Fixup.
Initialization effects on signal propagation, learning speed, or trainable depth.
Training above a learning-rate stability limit and curvature or sharpness behavior.
Deep neural networks, the listed MNIST/CIFAR-10/ImageNet settings, tolerance to higher learning rates, and Fixup without normalization.

rows.subject: TSK-MBGD-UR-BN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch normalization and uniform regularization; compared with TSK-MBGD-UR without batch normalization.
rows.baseline: TSK-MBGD-UR without BN; numerical baseline not stated
rows.value: BN resulted in smaller training losses; numerical values figure only
rows.uncertainty: Average over 10 repetitions; no error estimate stated
rows.note: The text describes the direction of the result; the plotted values are not given numerically.
rows.check: Smaller training losses with BN are explicitly reported, but for a TSK fuzzy classifier, outside V6's neural-network scope. The plotted comparison starts at epoch 3; numerical curve values cannot be recovered from the supplied text.

rows.subject: TSK-MBGD-UR-BN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with batch normalization and uniform regularization; compared with TSK-MBGD-UR without batch normalization.
rows.baseline: TSK-MBGD-UR without BN; numerical baseline not stated
rows.value: BN resulted in better generalization performances in testing; numerical values figure only
rows.uncertainty: Average over 10 repetitions; no error estimate stated
rows.note: The text describes the direction of the result; the plotted values are not given numerically.
rows.check: Better early test BCA is explicitly reported for a TSK fuzzy classifier. This does not establish V6 for neural networks, and test generalization alone does not establish faster training. The plotted comparison starts at epoch 3.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
